hints: Look first at the top diagram and then at the bar heights. The white clear area is where bacteria cannot grow, so which antibiotic number gives the biggest clear circle?
Remember the rule for this test: larger zone of inhibition in mm means more bacteria killed, so more effective. Smaller zone means less effective.
walkthrough:
**Understand what the zone means**

Think like the bacteria for a moment. Around the antibiotic disc there is a clear white circle with no growth. That is the zone of inhibition.

The bigger that clear zone, the more the antibiotic has stopped growth, so the more effective it is.

**Read the tallest and shortest bars**

Now read the bar chart of zone of inhibition / mm against antibiotic 1 to 5.

Antibiotic 3 has the tallest bar at about $22 \text{ mm}$. Antibiotic 2 has the shortest bar at about $4 \text{ mm}$. The others are in between: 1 is about $17 \text{ mm}$, 4 is about $19 \text{ mm}$, 5 is about $12 \text{ mm}$.

**Match to most and least effective**

Tallest bar means largest clear area means most killing, so most effective is 3.

Shortest bar means smallest clear area means least killing, so least effective is 2. That combination is option A.

options.A: Correct. Antibiotic 3 gives the largest zone (about 22 mm) so most effective, and antibiotic 2 gives the smallest zone (about 4 mm) so least effective.
options.B: Not correct. Antibiotic 4 is effective but its bar is shorter than 3, and 3 is the most effective not the least.
options.C: Half right only. 3 is most effective, but 1 has a medium zone of about 17 mm, not the smallest, so it is not least effective.
options.D: Reversed. 2 has the smallest zone so it is least effective, not most, and 3 has the largest zone so it is most effective, not least.
